subject: ACME - Rerank model fit validation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: ACME - Post-call recap: rerank goals & next steps

Hi Jordan 


Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goals: improve search result relevance for product pages (top-10) and reduce user re-search rate by 15%.
- Success metrics: NDCG@10 and MRR improvements on your holdout; guardrails for zero-quality regression on top traffic flows.
- Initial recommended model candidates: Llama-3-re-rank-small (quantized), OpenRerank-v2 (float16), and our Redwood-rerank-compact (tuned).

Next steps (proposed):
1) You share the 5k annotated impressions and the blind test split (thanks for uploading the CSV to the Drive folder).
2) We run a 2-week validation: baseline re-eval => candidate runs => compute NDCG/MRR; produce an A/B plan for canary.
3) Sales + Engineering sync to agree on rollout schedule and any privacy/retention constraints.

I've attached a short summary PDF with our initial NDCG/MRR estimates and the prompt set we propose to use. Aditya will follow up on the validation plan and A/B experiment design.

If that sounds right, can you confirm access to the dataset and a good SLA for sample returns (we typically ask for S3 or Drive access with read permissions within 48 hours)?

Thanks 
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

Subject: Re: ACME - Post-call recap: rerank goals & next steps (validation plan)

Jordan 

quick intro, I'm Aditya on the SE team. Appreciate the dataset access. High-level validation plan below (we'll share a reproducible notebook in the Drive folder):

1) Data ingestion & sanity checks (24-48h): verify labels, dedupe, bucket by traffic segments.
2) Baseline run: re-run your BM25 + pairwise model to get canonical metrics.
3) Candidate runs: Llama-3-re-rank-small (quantized), OpenRerank-v2 (fp16), Redwood-rerank-compact (tuned).
4) Metrics: NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, CTR-lift proxy, latency P50/P95. Also compute per-query traffic-weighted NDCG to surface regression on tail vs head queries.
5) Regression checks: fail-fast if any candidate drops traffic-weighted NDCG by >0.5% relative to baseline on top-traffic slice.
6) A/B plan: 2-week canary, 10k daily users, ramp 10% -> 50% if no regressions; kill switch with automatic rollback.

Attachments included: brief PDF with initial NDCG/MRR estimates and the prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl). We'll push the notebook and runner by EOD today.

If you have constraints on latency for serving at inference time, flag them now 
- we can prioritize the compact candidate.

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: ACME - initial validation results (NDCG/MRR summary)

Jordan 

quick update from the first pass (attached PDF has full tables):

- Baseline (BM25 + pairwise): NDCG@10 = 0.432, MRR = 0.381
- Llama-3-re-rank-small (quantized): NDCG@10 = 0.469 (+8.6%), MRR = 0.406 (+6.6%)
- OpenRerank-v2 (fp16): NDCG@10 = 0.476 (+10.2%), MRR = 0.415 (+8.9%)
- Redwood-rerank-compact: NDCG@10 = 0.462 (+7.0%), MRR = 0.399 (+4.8%)

Notes / concerns:
- We observed a small regression on a handful of tail queries for OpenRerank-v2 (per-query weighted NDCG drop ~0.9% for less-frequent queries). It's borderline with our fail-fast threshold.
- Latency: quantized Llama-3 candidate is fastest (P95 ~45ms), OpenRerank-v2 P95 ~120ms; Redwood-compact P95 ~60ms.

Next recommended steps:
- If latency is critical, prioritize Llama-3-re-rank-small canary.
- If max relevance lift is the goal and OpenRerank-v2 regressions are acceptable after targeted prompt tuning, run a targeted prompt/regression sweep on the tail queries before a wide canary.

I've attached the NDCG/MRR summary PDF and the prompt set we used. We're happy to run the targeted sweep 
- Aditya, can you propose the exact prompt variants and sample size for the tail-sweep?

Thanks 
Marissa

Attachment: acme_rerank_ndcg_mrr_summary.pdf
Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - initial validation results (A/B plan + tail sweep)

Jordan 

Suggested immediate plan based on the numbers Marissa shared:

1) Canary choice: Llama-3-re-rank-small at 10% traffic for 7 days (latency-friendly, strong lift).
2) Parallel tail sweep: run prompt variants on the ~300 tail queries where OpenRerank-v2 showed regression; sample 100 impressions/query to check stability (30k eval samples).
3) If tail sweep shows improvement, promote OpenRerank-v2 to a 10% canary for 7 days and compare against the Llama canary with the same traffic split (two-arm A/B).
4) Monitoring: daily NDCG@10, MRR, traffic-weighted NDCG, and latency SLAs. Auto-rollback if traffic-weighted NDCG drops >0.5% for 2 consecutive days.

Operational asks from ACME:
- Confirm the production traffic split mechanism (feature flag or weighted routing) and the contact for on-call rollback.
- Confirm whether we should include product facet filters in the evaluation (recommendation: yes, include top 5 facets to mirror production).

I'll push the prompt variant notebook and the A/B scheduler config to the Drive folder today. Once Jordan confirms, we'll schedule the canary start window (we prefer a weekday morning for monitoring).

- Aditya
